messages:
Maya (Support): heads up - multiple customers reporting sudden 50x/504 gateway errors hitting hosted generate endpoints since ~22:05 UTC. Most failures mention cache errors in gateway logs. Opening thread to coord investigation. Sample request id: req_02H7KQ4L. Viktor (Customer) is affected and asked for status.

Viktor (Customer): Yep we started seeing 502 -> 504s at 22:06. No code changes on our side. We use long-lived clients and retries; this looked like a backend failure. We have traces if needed.

Maya (Support): repro curl from affected org (sanitized):
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood-hosted.com/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXXX" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-3.8-redwood","input":"hello"}'

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
{ "error": "upstream memcached error: SERVER_ERROR" }
```

Maya (Support): gateway excerpt: 
```
22:07:02 gateway: req=req_02H7KQ4... svc=inference upstream=prefix-kv status=502 "upstream memcached error"
22:07:03 runtime: WARN prefix_cache.get org=org-987 key=org:987:pref err="connection refused"
22:07:03 runtime: WARN prefix_cache.get latency=610ms
```

Tomas (SRE): pulling memcached-prod metrics now. I see connection count spikes at 22:04-22:12, server errors, and increase in `conn_create_failures`. p95 op latency spiked to ~450ms, p99 ~1.1s on memcached-n2. Also unusual: file-descriptor usage high on the memcached fleet.

Priya (Eng - infra): We deployed a low-overhead telemetry agent to memcached cluster at 21:58 to gather per-key sizes (rolling canary). Looks like agent made many short-lived connections concurrently; combined with our default client behavior (no connection pooling in some runtime shards) we caused connection churn. Rolling the agent back now.

Lin (Eng - runtime): Oof. Our prefix cache client had a recent change that disabled persistent sockets under heavy load in certain goroutines due to a mistaken `defer conn.Close()` in the fastpath PR. That increases connection creation significantly. I'm preparing a hotfix to restore pooling.

Zoe (Platform): Immediate mitigations we can do now: 1) flip runtime feature `cache.prefer_local=false` (i.e., prefer-direct model calls) to bypass prefix cache for hosted; 2) enable stale-serve: allow runtime to serve last-known value for prefix cache misses for 5s (stale-while-revalidate) so we don't block on KV fetch; 3) increase memcached connection limit on frontend load-balancers temporarily. Which do we want first?

Tomas (SRE): Start with bypass toggle + LB conn limit. Bypass will stop the synchronous dependency; LB change buys time while infra rollback completes. I'll also open an alert to detect fd exhaustion earlier.

Zoe (Platform): Flipping bypass flag for hosted now via feature API:
```
POST https://console.internal/api/flags
{"flag":"bypass_prefix_kv","env":"hosted","value":true}
Response: 200 OK
```
deploy-bot: deployment acknowledged: toggle-reconfiguration job queued (job-7781)

Lin (Eng - runtime): Patch for client pooling prepared and building. I also pushed a temporary change to runtime to enable `serve_stale_prefix=true` (hotfix) so requests don't wait for KV for 2nd-level lookups. Logs will annotate `prefix_cache.mode=bypass|stale`.

Maya (Support): Notifying customers (Viktor and others) that we're actively mitigating and to expect fewer errors in next 60-90s.

Viktor (Customer): Re-tested at 22:11. We see success responses now (200s). We'll keep monitoring for 30m. Thank you.

Tomas (SRE): After bypass + lb change: gateway 5xx rate down from ~7.9% -> 0.9% in 2 minutes. Memcached connections still high but dropping after rollback started.

Priya (Eng - infra): rollback of telemetry agent completed at 22:14. memcached-n2 fd and conn metrics returning toward baseline. We'll keep an eye for any node reboots.

Lin (Eng - runtime): Hotfix merged to restore persistent pooling + reduce per-shard ephemeral connections. Rolling to runtime shards over the next 10m. Patch link: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pulls/4923

deploy-bot: runtime rollout started: rollout-id=rr-4923 stage=canary

Tomas (SRE): Canary telemetry: client connection creations down 95% on patched shards, memcached p99 read latency down to normal ~30ms. Gateway error rate back to baseline.

Maya (Support): Customer confirmation: Viktor reports 0 errors in last 10m. I'll close the customer-impact loop and file follow-ups.

Lin (Eng - runtime): Proposed permanent actions: 
- revert the accidental `conn.Close()` regression and add unit tests for connection reuse (Lin) - PR in 24h
- add circuit-breaker at runtime cache client to fail-open when memcached p95 > 200ms (Lin/Tomas) - 48h
- implement per-org large-key sampler to detect and quiesce heavy-prefix writers (Priya) - design 72h
- add feature-runbook for cache bypass toggles + automated rollback (Zoe) - doc + script 24h
- add fd/conn prealert for memcached fleet (Tomas) - alert in 12h

Maya (Support): I'll link this thread into ticket SUP-9019 and send customer summary. Thanks everyone for quick response. :clap:

note: thread includes root message and chronological replies; logs and code snippets included for repro and mitigation
note: Slack thread JSON per agents.md: single continuous messages string, required metadata present
